rounds.answer:
The exact current marker is INTERVIEW-41-698a12f2ce9470fd. The task is daily-temperatures, with the JavaScript interface solve(temperatures).

Use a monotonic stack of unresolved day indices and initialize all results to zero. Scan left to right: while the current temperature is strictly greater than the temperature at the stack’s top index, pop that index and record the difference in indices; then push the current index.

The invariant is that stack indices increase and their temperatures are non-increasing; every stacked day is still waiting for its first strictly warmer day. When a day is popped, the current day is its first warmer day because any earlier warmer day would already have resolved it. Each index is pushed and popped at most once, giving O(n) time and O(n) space.

Empty input returns an empty array. A single day, equal temperatures, or a non-increasing sequence leaves unresolved entries at zero; equal temperatures never count as warmer.

Marker: INTERVIEW-42-ad4ce5290621b378.

Use a monotonic stack of unresolved indices and initialize every result to -1. Scan the array twice using circular indexing. Whenever the current value is strictly greater than the value at the stack’s top index, pop that index and set its answer to the current value. Push indices only during the first pass; the second pass resolves wraparound matches.

Invariant: stack indices represent unanswered elements, with values non-increasing from bottom to top. Each popped element receives its first strictly greater value in circular traversal order; equal values never resolve each other.

Boundary cases: empty input returns []; a singleton or all-equal array returns only -1. Maximum values remain -1, and decreasing arrays require wraparound—for example, [3, 2, 1] gives [-1, 3, 3]. Negative values work with the same strict comparison.

Time: O(n), since each index is pushed and popped at most once. Space: O(n).

For solve(asteroids), scan left to right using a stack of survivors. A collision occurs only when the stack top is positive and the incoming asteroid is negative: pop smaller positive tops and continue checking; on equal magnitudes, remove the top and discard the incoming asteroid; against a larger top, discard the incoming asteroid. Push the incoming asteroid only if it survives.

Invariant: after each input, the stack contains the surviving asteroids from the processed prefix, in original order, with no unresolved collisions.

Boundary cases include empty input, a single asteroid, all asteroids moving the same direction, separating pairs such as [-2, 3], equal collisions such as [3, -3], and chain collisions such as [3, 5, -6], which leaves [-6].
